title: Domain-scoped MCP servers on SAP BTP for Joule agents
problem: Give Joule agents governed, reliable access to S/4HANA business functions.
depth: Architecture path and design rules stated by the implementer; no measured results
technologies_stated: MCP servers on BTP Cloud Foundry
facts: Path: Joule Studio agent to MCP server on Cloud Foundry to Destination service to Cloud Connector to S/4HANA.
Authentication is OAuth2 client credentials, with CSRF handling for OData V2 and one shared destination for all servers.
Nine MCP servers with 144 tools, each scoped to one business domain, about 20-30 tools per server.
The author cites reduced tool-selection accuracy with large tool sets as the reason for narrow servers.
The author reads a recent SAP API policy as requiring agent calls to SAP APIs to go through SAP-endorsed paths and notes unresolved customer questions.
interpretations: Client-credentials auth implies service-level identity; the post describes no per-user authorisation, so segregation of duties would need separate design.
The SAP API policy statement is the author's reading and must be verified against SAP's own text before use.

decisions.selected: One server per business domain, ~20-30 tools
decisions.alternatives: One large server for all APIs
decisions.reasoning: Author cites tool-selection degradation as tool count grows.

decisions.selected: Reuse BTP Destination and Cloud Connector
decisions.alternatives: Direct network exposure of S/4HANA; custom connectivity
decisions.reasoning: Author states it keeps within SAP's existing trust layer.

decisions.alternatives: Principal propagation or on-behalf-of user tokens
decisions.reasoning: Not discussed by the source; comparison is independent analysis.

review_exercise: Find the segregation-of-duties risk in this architecture and redesign identity so the agent cannot exceed the user's authorisations.
adaptation: Template for exposing Commerce or Service Cloud APIs to Joule agents. Independent analysis.
